P.note: Most complete and physically coherent account of color-in-material (solid vs hollow parts deepening with thickness, darker overlaps, blue caustic shadow on a white plinth), with blue-tinted overexposure balanced against a sky that stays saturated, all phrased positively and front-loaded.

Q.note: Strong backlit dyed-through-plastic description and a distinctive Y2K inflatable-vinyl cushion idea, but the #3CFF2E grass risks radioactive neon, the edges drift to aqua, and 'high dynamic range' works against the overexposed look.

R.note: Rich material detail, but it front-loads 'electric-cyan acrylic' instead of blue, swaps the vinyl cushions for frosted silicone (a step toward generic frosted glass), and names the Windows XP Bliss wallpaper outright.

S.note: Covers every brief element correctly and cleanly, including the hollow-shell rim logic, but it is so compressed and telegraphic, with no camera or color anchors, that it gives the model less to work with.

T.note: Vivid and tangible (mold seams, scuffs, overlap density), but 'tropical water', cyan rims and frosted-white silicone cushions pull it off the blue acrylic-and-vinyl brief, and it asks the model to imitate the Bliss wallpaper.

U.note: Faithful and well-formed, but generic in places: filler like 'ultra-detailed' and 'gentle lens flare', a silver driver that brings in metal, and pure-neon #39FF3A grass.
